target_customer: Engineering hiring teams that want to measure how candidates use AI coding agents
problem: Engineers now write code with AI agents, but hiring tests still assess unaided coding. Saffron lets candidates build features in a real repository with Claude Code and scores the session.
business_model: B2B SaaS assessment platform with demo led sales (pricing not found)
product_category: HR tech, AI native technical assessments

founders.name: Kazuma Choji
education: Harvey Mudd, computer science and math
founders.background_notes: Published at NeurIPS and ICML, per the YC page, which also lists an ICCV authorship.

competitors.name: CodeSignal
competitors.what: Added AI assisted coding assessments and interviews

competitors.name: HackerRank
competitors.what: AI assisted interviews where interviewers watch candidates use an AI assistant

competitors.name: CoderPad
competitors.what: Interview platform arguing signal now comes from how candidates work with AI

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser IDE on a company repo with agent sessions, replay and multi agent scoring is standard engineering with some hard parts in scoring reliability.

defensibility.rationale: Incumbents added the same feature in 2026, and the product is copyable. Customer repos and rubrics may add some lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: All three had already shipped AI assisted assessments or interviews by early 2026, the same wedge.

market_need_then: AI coding agents changed daily engineering work in 2025 and 2026, so employers question unaided coding tests; incumbents responded with AI assisted formats.

identity.logo: Standard and white logo files; design not described
identity.mascot_or_character: Dithered saffron flower graphic used throughout the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, contrasting taglines such as Good code is easy now. Good engineers aren't.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct flower imagery and clear voice, but a common word shared by many companies and no press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Saffron is a three person Spring 2026 YC company selling AI native engineering assessments, backed by YC and Afore Capital. The founders have Jane Street and strong CS backgrounds, but CodeSignal, HackerRank and CoderPad shipped similar features first. No outcome exists yet, so the key risk is incumbent copying.
notes: Aggregators (Caplight, FundedIQ) list a 500K USD pre-seed dated 2026-06 with Afore Capital as co-investor; seen only on aggregators and the YC page names Afore without an amount, so the amount is unverified and not recorded as a round. Afore Capital backing is confirmed by the YC page. Outcome search found no Saffron news, only unrelated hiring companies. Added a pre-seed round dated 2026-06 that rests on a single database (VCBacked, no amount). The 500K amount from Caplight and FundedIQ stays unverified and is not recorded; a second search found no source giving an amount.
